title: Workout Scale Values
prompt: A workout preview applies the same multiplier to every rep count. Write a function that returns a new array with every value multiplied by the factor.

explanation.beginner:
Example: workoutScaleValues([1,2,3], 4) produces [4,8,12]. Project each included record into the requested output shape, keeping the required input order.

Compare “handles zero factor”: input [[4,5],0] produces [0,0]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Project each included record into the requested output shape, keeping the required input order.

Tempting mistake: A projection is different from filtering: returning a boolean from map gives booleans, while returning a value from filter only makes a keep decision.

The reference uses map. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles zero factor”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
